parent_statement: Priority Action #4 - Greening Hotels and Resorts
policy_statement: Create a coordination framework for hotel/resort sustainability, including incentives, regulation, GHG monitoring and awareness activities.
source_quote: From the detailed description of issues at stake, the priority action will draw strategic priorities with a double objective in mind - improve hotels/ resorts sustainable operation in the City of Luxor, while reducing the environmental foot print of the tourism facilities. This could include: - Establish a coordination unit to manage this priority action plan engaging with stakeholders to support a change of mind set in hotels and resorts managers, highlighting the benefits of a greener profile,
extraction_rationale: Governance and implementation package for hotel/resource-efficiency action.

parent_statement: Priority Action #4 - Greening Hotels and Resorts
policy_statement: Develop solar water heating in hotels and resorts, supported by a revolving fund for phased investment.
source_quote: Component 2: Develop Solar Water Heating in hotel and resorts Hotels and resorts need water for their visitors and their equipment (swimming pool). Solar is easy solution to warm water. Any hotel/ resort, with 200 rooms will need around 50.000 litres per day half of it been warm enough for sanitary use and washing (towels, sheets, soils).
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable-heat intervention; surrounding text establishes revolving fund support.

parent_statement: Priority Action #4 - Greening Hotels and Resorts
policy_statement: Develop or further assess solar water heating for floating hotels.
source_quote: Component 3: Develop Solar Water Heating in floating hotels For the 275 floating hotels representing 16,000 rooms meaning 2 thirds of the overall capacity in Luxor. If we assume each floating hotel would accommodate 60 rooms in average we would have a maximum of 120 guests plus 30 staff: 150 per floating hotel.
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable-heat measure for floating hotels, with implementation conditional on ROI.

parent_statement: Priority Action #4 - Greening Hotels and Resorts
policy_statement: Supply natural gas to hotels and resorts on Luxor's eastern bank after prioritizing solar water heating and energy efficiency.
source_quote: Component 4: Hotels/Resorts natural gas supply The City of Luxor is developing its natural gas grid and would like to connect as many hotels as possible. Note that in merit order, renewable comes first (SWH), gas comes next and last comes diesel.
extraction_rationale: Cleaner-fuel infrastructure action with mitigation framing.

policy_statement: Implement Priority Action #5, the Green Governorate Buildings Plan, to reduce energy use and GHG emissions in public buildings.
source_quote: Phase 2: Develop a specific programme 'Green Governorate Buildings plan' - GGBP, mobilising managers and staff. This plan should focus on the following measures:
extraction_rationale: Named building-sector priority action with efficiency and renewable-energy sub-actions.

parent_statement: Priority Action #5 - Green Governorate Buildings Plan
policy_statement: Create an EAU-supported behavioral energy-saving program for Governorate buildings.
source_quote:
Component 1: Phase 1: Setting up the EAU - Allocating staff - Installing basic equipment.

Phase 2: Develop a specific programme 'Green Governorate Buildings plan' - GGBP, mobilising managers and staff. This plan should focus on the following measures:
extraction_rationale: Institutional and behavioral efficiency program under the public-building parent action.

parent_statement: Priority Action #5 - Green Governorate Buildings Plan
policy_statement: Replace old lamps and air conditioners in Governorate buildings and install energy efficient systems.
source_quote: Component 2: Beyond promoting awareness and behavioural change, it is necessary to develop a clear and comprehensive plan to replace old devices (lamps and air conditioners) and equipment and install energy efficient systems that will help in reducing electricity consumption. Ideally, this programme should be implemented, in a first phase, in a small number of buildings (starting with the more symbolic one: the main Governor's building or city hall), but covering all type of devices and equipment, in order to concentrate many initiatives on the selected buildings and demonstrate the benefit of these structural changes.
extraction_rationale: Specific retrofit program with named equipment categories and phased implementation.

parent_statement: Priority Action #5 - Green Governorate Buildings Plan
policy_statement: Install 8,500 LED lamps and motion sensors in public buildings at an estimated cost of €40,000.
source_quote:
Switch to LED lamps and sensor systems

Replacing lamps in all public buildings with LED devices, would require installing 8,500 LED lamps (1 lamp per 10 square meters over 50% of the entire building area of 175,500 m 2 ). This would cost 30,600 for buying lamps

+ 9,400 for sensors hence a total investment of 40,000 € (822,000 EGP).
section_header: Switch to LED lamps and sensor systems
extraction_rationale: Quantified equipment and cost for an energy-efficiency intervention.

parent_statement: Priority Action #5 - Green Governorate Buildings Plan
policy_statement: Switch 50% of Governorate buildings from reverse AC/heating systems to central cooling/heating management.
source_quote:
Switching to more efficient AC devices

Switch from AC/Heating reverse systems to central management of cooling/heating in 50% of these buildings is estimated 150.000 €. This will generate savings of 987 MWh/y (30% reduction on 70% of global electricity consumption in public buildings) avoiding a cost of 35,450 €/y (730,380 EGP) allowing a 4,5 years payback.
section_header: Switching to more efficient AC devices
extraction_rationale: Quantified cooling/heating energy-efficiency measure.

parent_statement: Priority Action #5 - Green Governorate Buildings Plan
policy_statement: Install an initial 7,500 kWp of solar PV on Governorate buildings.
source_quote:
Having 150,700 square meters of roofs available from Governorate's buildings in the City of Luxor and assuming 60% of these roofs can be used, we would have 90,500 square meters for Solar PV installation, meaning a capacity to install 12,500 kWp - a global investment of 16 million € for a potential production of 22,500 MWh/y.

The priority action #5 recommends a staged approach with a first round tapping on 50% of the entire potential, meaning installing 7,500 kWp: for example, 50 units of 100 kWp and 10 units of 250 kWp.
extraction_rationale: Quantified renewable-electricity target for public buildings.

parent_statement: Priority Action #5 - Green Governorate Buildings Plan
policy_statement: Install solar water heating systems in 100 Governorate buildings, with five units per building.
source_quote:
Developing Solar Water Heating systems

Such systems can be used to cover hot water needs in any buildings. There use is even more interesting in schools, mosques, and hospitals with higher requirements for hot water.

The priority action #5 propose to equip develop 100 buildings with 5 SWH units of 3 collectors.
extraction_rationale: Quantified renewable-heat deployment target.

policy_statement: Establish a Green tourism support unit and investment fund to advise hotels and resorts on energy efficiency and renewable energy and provide attractive-rate loans.
source_quote:
To shift behaviour and speed up the shift, the Governorate should establish a ' Green tourism support unit ' providing advices to tourism operators willing to invest in energy efficiency and renewable energy. This technical unit will ensure audits to any resort and hotel willing to make necessary investments to contribute to the SECAP adopted in the City of Luxor - Governorate of Luxor.

The technical unit could also set up an investment fund that would help resorts and hotels doing the right
extraction_rationale: Named support unit and financing mechanism for tourism energy transition.

policy_statement: Create a Green boat refurbishment fund and upgrade cruise boats through modern engines and rooftop solar PV.
source_quote:
The Governorate of Luxor could facilitate the establishment of ' Green boat refurbishment fund ' that could be replenished by tourist operators benefiting from loans or subsidies to upgrade their boat. Note that modern engines could dramatically reduce energy consumption.

Some on board functions and services could also be supplied only from renewable electricity produced with solar PV installed on the rooftop of cruise boats.
extraction_rationale: Named fund and specific vessel upgrade measures.

policy_statement: Establish a Green dock programme using solar PV to supply river-dock activities and docking boats.
source_quote: The fleet improvement programme should extend to redesigning the docks to make them a demonstrative example of what a 'green harbour' on river Nile could be. Obviously the new plans should promote solar PV equipment as a major source of renewable energy supply for all activities along the docks.
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable-energy infrastructure intervention for river docks.

policy_statement: Establish a green tourist transport line using electric or biogas buses between central Luxor hotels and major heritage sites.
source_quote: One option would be to establish a 'green transport line' between the City centre of Luxor, where most hotels are and the most important heritage sites such as Luxor temple, Karnak temple, Valley of the King, using electric buses or biogas ones would be a nice symbol of Luxor switching to renewable energy. This would be the great come back of the 'sun' at the centre of City of Gods!
extraction_rationale: Specific low-carbon tourist transport intervention.

policy_statement: Assess and modernize heritage-site lighting to reduce nighttime electricity consumption while maintaining necessary service.
source_quote: Heritage sites and tourist attractions consume 24.3 GWh/year in electricity. This consumption is mainly due to lighting sites in the evening and at night. It is hard to understand why heritage sites should be lighted up at night.
extraction_rationale: Specific assessment and lighting-efficiency intervention for heritage sites; somewhat less developed than other measures but has a clear energy-consumption target area.

policy_statement: Run a residential energy-awareness campaign promoting thermostat settings, efficient behavior, efficient appliances, elevator limits and window films.
source_quote:
Such awareness campaign to promote efficient behaviour should focus on few measures:

- -Promoting the proper temperature at home: using excessive air' cooling is not good for public health and result in huge electricity consumption. Adjusting air conditioning systems' thermostats to be always at 24 degrees Celsius in summer would save up to 25 per cent of the energy consumption,
section_header: 4.2.3.2 Short-term actions (3 to 5 years time frame)
extraction_rationale: Specific residential energy-efficiency awareness action with named measures and quantified savings potential.

policy_statement: Promote residential solar water heating to replace electric water heating, including company training and service-fee models.
source_quote:
The most obvious plan to develop on the medium term is the promotion of Solar Heating System to produce hot sanitary water and avoid unnecessary electricity consumption.

- -Promote the use of solar water heating (SWH) system instead of the current electric water heating (EWH) systems.
section_header: 4.2.3.3 Medium-term actions (3 to 10 years' time frame)
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable-heat and electricity-saving intervention.

policy_statement: Develop a residential building energy-retrofitting programme with mapping, local-company training, third-party bank financing, showcases, efficient cooling, solar PV and green roofs.
source_quote:
On the long term, it would be necessary to develop a renovation programme targeting less energy efficient building where basic insulation could significantly improve comfort while reducing energy consumption.

To design and implement an adequate energy-retrofitting plan for residential buildings, the Governorate of Luxor should engage in the following steps:
section_header: 4.2.3.4 Long-term actions (5 to 15 years time frame)
extraction_rationale: Concrete long-term retrofit programme with specified implementation steps.

policy_statement: Assess tertiary buildings and run entrepreneur-focused awareness, technical support and recognition for energy-efficiency investments.
source_quote:
It is necessary to add a first step to properly assess the need through a detailed mapping of tertiary buildings, (schools and religious buildings), registering average energy consumption per square meter, date of construction, location. This will help targeting buildings offering the best potential for saving.

Hence, the action plan could be structured with two components:
extraction_rationale: Specific tertiary-building mapping and efficiency support action.

policy_statement: Develop energy-efficiency and renewable-energy partnerships for non-commercial service buildings, hospitals, mosques and churches.
source_quote:
- -The Governorate should develop partnerships with some of these 'service providers' to develop showcases of efficient building also using renewable energy,
- -Promote energy efficiency in hospitals and health centres, offering the possibility for these institutions to use saving for re-investing in improving their capacity to deliver services, and
- -Engage a partnership with priests and imams to develop energy efficient devices and renewable energy in mosques and churches.
extraction_rationale: Concrete tertiary/service building efficiency and renewable-energy programme.

policy_statement: Organize crop-residue and bio-waste collection for processing in bio-digesters to produce biogas, electricity, heat or vehicle fuel.
source_quote: As agriculture in the Governorate of Luxor produces a large amount of waste from harvesting, recycling such residues should be a top priority. The option would be to organize the collection of crop residues and combine this material with other bio-waste from other sources (food waste from hotel and resorts) to process it in bio-digesters.
extraction_rationale: Specific agricultural waste-to-energy intervention.

policy_statement: Develop industrial energy audits and awareness campaigns to reduce industry energy consumption and promote renewable energy solutions.
source_quote: One practical option would be to develop energy audits for companies willing to address energy issues. This approach will help entrepreneurs considering the importance of energy in their business model and its impact on their profitability. When they will have understood how important is the subject, they will be keen to engage actions to reduce their energy consumption and when possible and appropriate to develop renewable energy production capacities.
section_header: 4.2.6.2 Short-term actions (3 to 5 years' time frame)
extraction_rationale: Specific industrial energy-audit and renewable-energy promotion intervention.

policy_statement: Create a Green Industry Unit to support industry and service energy audits, process efficiency, rooftop renewable energy, and waste reduction/recycling.
source_quote: The 'Green Industry Unit' initially set up to offer services to Industry' operators could progressively expend its support to the service sector (tertiary buildings) and the industry. This technical unit would provide advices and technical support to any company willing to seriously address any issues regarding energy consumption or production.
section_header: 4.2.6.3 Long-term action (5 to 15 years' time frame)
extraction_rationale: Named support unit with efficiency, renewable-energy and recycling functions.

policy_statement: Partner with Terra Sola to develop solar PV on Governorate buildings, symbolic buildings, parking lots, bus stations and households.
source_quote:
As Terra Sola also plans to establish a dedicated fund to developing and supporting small and medium-sized renewable energy projects in Luxor, the Governorate of Luxor should develop a partnership with this company targeting different objectives:

- -Develop solar PV units on all Governorate buildings : Potential of Solar PV equipment has been explored for various public buildings and a first experiment seems to be very promising (conducted in 4 public buildings in Luxor);
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable-energy partnership and deployment package, with fund reference.

policy_statement: Set up a City of Luxor revolving fund to support residential and private-owner solar PV deployment.
source_quote: The plan would be to develop solar PV units in every possible place invited inhabitants to contribute to this development. Through this process, city residents will benefit additional income after the payback period and will become energy producers as well as being energy consumers. The City of Luxor could set up a revolving fund to support this development.
section_header: Solar PV for residents and private owners
extraction_rationale: Financial instrument supporting small-scale renewable electricity.

policy_statement: Promote solar heating across households, tourism, industry, shops and restaurants through awareness, needs assessment, technical solutions and pilot projects.
source_quote: Solar heating could be widely used for covering households' needs and tourism sector heat consumption (for sanitary water and swimming pools). Solar heating could also be used in some industries, shops, restaurants, etc. that require hot water. Modern equipment is allowing very good performance to match specific industrial needs.
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable-heat technology promotion programme.

policy_statement: Commission a €20,000 comprehensive study on bio-digesters for agricultural by-products and organic waste.
source_quote: As previously mentioned, there is a huge potential in agricultural by products and organic waste to be processed in bio-digesters. The Governorate of Luxor should command a comprehensive study to explore the benefit of such a technology in the surrounding of the City. This study would be the basis to recommend the most appropriate set up: number of units and size; bio-waste collection system; energy production expected and recommended use (heat, electricity or fuel for vehicles).
extraction_rationale: Specific study with cost estimate for renewable-energy production from waste.

policy_statement: Conduct a €20,000 prefeasibility study on adapting hydro turbines in the Nile River near Luxor.
source_quote:
Such hydro turbine would produce electricity that could nicely combine with solar, as the Nile River doesn't stop at night when solar PV will not be active anymore.

A 20.000 Euro prefeasibility study could give enough information to decide if the Governorate of Luxor should proceed with this technology or not.
extraction_rationale: Specific renewable-energy feasibility study with budget.

policy_statement: Develop a heat and extreme-event health action plan, monitoring systems and regional medical collaboration.
source_quote: Health action plan for the extreme events: This is mainly about improving monitoring systems to ensure that any disease development will be detected early and addressed by competent public health services in the Governorate. This plan is currently under development. To optimise reactivity, in the event of a problem, a collaborative approach with the regional medical services has been developed.
extraction_rationale: Adaptation plan for climate-related extreme events and public-health risks.

policy_statement: Improve public sheltering capacity through climate-friendly air conditioning in public services for extreme heat and other extreme weather events.
source_quote: Improve sheltering capacities : Improve air conditioning in public services (hospitals, city hall, etc.) using climate friendly options to offer appropriate extreme heat protection to those citizens that lack the infrastructure to protect themselves. Such sites should also be considered as potential shelters when other type of extreme weather events will affect the more vulnerable groups (storms, floods).
extraction_rationale: Specific resilience intervention for heat, storms and floods.

policy_statement: Set up an early warning system for heat waves, fires, floods and other natural disasters, with an estimated annual budget of €50,000.
source_quote:
Developing an early warning system, to alert citizens in the case of extreme weather events or natural disasters such as heat waves, fires, floods, etc. is vital. This system needs to be set up as early as possible connecting with national monitoring centres to be able to transmit appropriate information as early as possible to citizen of Luxor.

This should be established as early as possible and would require a budget of about 50.000 € / year.
extraction_rationale: Specific warning system with named hazards and annual budget.

policy_statement: Launch educational and awareness campaigns on heat waves, floods and vector-borne diseases, with an estimated annual budget of €30,000.
source_quote:
Educational and awareness raising campaigns should be developed to inform people about health impacts of heat waves, floods, vector borne diseases, etc., and educate residents on the ways to protect their health and prevent infection or disease outbreaks.

This should be launched as early as possible and would require a budget of about 30.000 € / year.
extraction_rationale: Specific public-health adaptation campaign with hazards and budget.

policy_statement: Mitigate disease outbreak risk through city cleanliness maintenance, sewage and drainage quality control, and mapping disease hot spots.
source_quote: Mitigate risk of disease outbreak through appropriate maintenance of the city's cleanliness, as well as regular quality control of sewage and drainage systems. Indeed sewage, waste dumps and dormant waters are reservoirs for serious diseases. Unless the City services fix these components, health risks will remains high in the city.
extraction_rationale: Technical adaptation measure for disease risks linked to sanitation and extreme conditions.

policy_statement: Improve water quality control to ensure availability during heat waves and reduce disease-spreading risks.
source_quote: Improving water quality control is also necessary as water availability is essential. First, to cover the basic needs of people particularly during periods of heat waves. Secondly, because it can be a vehicle for spreading diseases if quality control is not sufficient.
extraction_rationale: Adaptation measure tied directly to heat waves and disease prevention.

policy_statement: Design a Water and Waste Water management plan to manage water flux during heavy rains and urban runoff.
source_quote: Water and Waste Water management plan is under design as part of this SECAP (refer to Section III, part 4.1.4 / p.37). This plan is must to ensure proper management of water flux particularly in the case of heavy rains that could overpass absorption capacities of the current system. This plan also needs to consider artificialized areas that will speed up water run-off.
extraction_rationale: Specific plan for heavy-rain and runoff adaptation.

policy_statement: Improve monitoring of bridges and docksides and design new specifications to withstand high waters and floods.
source_quote: Improve infrastructure monitoring , particularly for bridges and docksides to anticipate any problems that would undermine their resistance to high waters and floods. The adequate process should be set up to ensure that any problem identified will result in an immediate remediation process. This also means designing new specifications for bridges and docksides to match the maximum expected flow during extreme events.
extraction_rationale: Infrastructure monitoring and standards action for climate resilience.

policy_statement: Model predicted electricity demand and supply to avoid blackouts during heat waves and climate-affected solar PV performance.
source_quote: Modelling predicted demand and supply in electricity to adapt production capacities to actual requirements. Heat waves will increase the demand as well as degrading performance of solar PV. It is then key to develop models that will ensure a perfect match between demand and supply to avoid blackout when people are in particular need of electricity.
extraction_rationale: Electricity reliability adaptation measure for heat waves.

policy_statement: Establish underground water reservoirs and a flood control system to manage heavy rain runoff and Nile River levels.
source_quote: Establish underground water reservoirs and develop a flood control system . Reservoirs are necessary to retain water in case of heavy rains. Such reservoirs should be located in strategic areas where water gets channelled. Reservoir will retain water and avoid dramatic run off that could cause adverse impacts to the built environment downstream.
extraction_rationale: Specific flood-risk adaptation infrastructure measure.

policy_statement: Upgrade riverside defence systems and re-engineer docksides to increase their height near affected facilities.
source_quote: Upgrade of riverside defence systems near potentially affected facilities and conduct potential re-engineering to increase the height of docksides. This could be done along the plan to reorganize docksides and install solar PV, as mentioned in this SECAP Section III (refer to part 4.2.2 - Tourism sector, page 42).
extraction_rationale: Concrete flood/high-water defence measure; source explicitly mentions solar PV as a linked mitigation component.

policy_statement: Modify building codes to promote more energy-efficient and heat-tolerant structures, including Nubian Vault demonstration buildings.
source_quote: Modify the building codes to promote more energy efficient and heat tolerant structures. Upper Egypt has been the place where very efficient building techniques has been developed in the old times. The Nubian Vault is one these techniques only requiring mud and clay (no cement, no wood, and no iron) to elaborate on buildings that are particularly well adapted to hot regions.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory code-change adaptation and efficiency measure.

policy_statement: Provide municipal tax reductions for households adopting climate adaptation measures.
source_quote: Set up incentives for innovative climate friendly buildings. This could be done, for example, through the provision of reductions on the municipal taxes for those proceeding in adoption of adaptation measures in their houses.
extraction_rationale: Financial incentive/tax reduction for adaptation measures.

policy_statement: Develop integrated land-use planning and zoning for risk-exposed areas, protection infrastructure, innovative building methods, biodiversity preservation, and mitigation/adaptation objectives.
source_quote: Develop an integrated land use planning with zoning system depending on the different areas exposed to risk, dedicated to protection infrastructures or areas, and/or to innovative building methods. This land planning should take into account the three most important element of pressure that combines in the City of Luxor: growing urbanisation, tourism around heritage sites, requirement to preserve agricultural lands.
extraction_rationale: Planning and zoning intervention for climate risk exposure and sustainable land use.

policy_statement: Develop green roofs, green walls, trees, green areas and fountains to increase shade and reduce the heat island effect.
source_quote:
Develop greening infrastructure such as buildings' roofs and walls covered with greenery to increase the amount of shade and refresh the environment.

The very presence of trees and plants generates a cooling effect on the immediate environment. Such structures could be promoted initially in public buildings as a demonstration of the benefits.
extraction_rationale: Ecosystem-based urban cooling measure addressing heat.

policy_statement: Build exemplary districts with climate-friendly and climate-adapted urban forms, greenery, white roofs, natural shading and bioclimatic design.
source_quote: Build exemplary districts with climate friendly and climate adapted urban forms and buildings. The combination of innovative technics (including the Nubian Vault mentioned above), adequate district design and greenery development could result in a much appreciated urban environment. Other techniques such as using white roofs, natural shading and bioclimatic designs, could be integrated in these exemplary districts.
extraction_rationale: District-scale adaptation and urban-design intervention.

policy_statement: Promote agricultural climate adaptation plans using drip irrigation, agro-forestry systems and drought-resistant crops.
source_quote: Promote agriculture climate adaptation plans . It would be interesting to promote technologies that will both favour climate mitigation and adaptation: drip irrigation practices, agro-forestry systems, drought resistant crops, etc. This should be done in conjunction with mitigation measures that are promoted in this SECAP.
extraction_rationale: Sectoral adaptation action with named measures and explicit mitigation co-benefit.

policy_statement: Protect biodiversity by planting native trees along the Nile, protecting riverside biodiversity, restoring riparian buffers and preserving desert biodiversity.
source_quote: Protect the biodiversity . This programme should include tree planning (using native species) alongside the Nile River and riverside biodiversity protection. It should aim to establish and restore riparian buffers.
extraction_rationale: Biodiversity and riparian restoration program using ecosystems as resilience infrastructure.

policy_statement: Implement Al-Qurna Priority Action #2, Clear transportation on the west bank, to reorganize parking, extend microbus routes, use solar sheds, convert microbuses to natural gas, and plan bicycle lanes and electric cars.
source_quote:
5.1.2 Clear transportation on the west bank

Al-Qurna - Priority action # 2 for SECAP
section_header: 5.1.2 Clear transportation on the west bank
extraction_rationale: Named SECAP priority action in the Al-Qurna annex with multiple transport and renewable-energy sub-actions.

parent_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #2 - Clear transportation on the west bank
policy_statement: Install 20 kW solar panel sheds to power waiting-area air conditioning and connect them to the national grid.
source_quote: Component 3: Set solar panel sheds to power the waiting area's ACs with a capacity of 20kW and connect it to the national grid (give and take system). (If the location is close enough to the Tourist Information Centre, it could be able to provide electricity from sheds).
extraction_rationale: Quantified solar PV installation for transport infrastructure.

parent_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #2 - Clear transportation on the west bank
policy_statement: Equip four Bo'irat-serving microbuses with natural gas engines and plan conversion of all West Bank microbuses to natural gas.
source_quote:
Component 2: Equip 4 of the microbuses, those who will be serving Bo'irat village, with natural gas engines.

Component 3: Set a plan to convert all the microbuses on the West Bank from the already expensive gasoline into natural gas engines (project second phase).
extraction_rationale: Quantified low-carbon fuel-switching action with follow-on fleet plan.

parent_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #2 - Clear transportation on the west bank
policy_statement: Partner with the traffic department to enforce mandatory natural-gas conversion when renewing vehicle licenses.
source_quote:
The traffic department (MoI) could partner enforcing a mandatory conversion to use a natural gas based engine when renewing the vehicle license.

Phase 2

Develop a plan to a future extension of to adopt bicycle lanes, and usage of electric cars.
extraction_rationale: Regulatory fuel-conversion mechanism; wording is tentative because it says 'could partner'.

parent_statement: Al-Qurna Priority Action #2 - Clear transportation on the west bank
policy_statement: Plan future bicycle lanes, electric-car use and booster charging from new PV systems.
source_quote:
Phase 2

Develop a plan to a future extension of to adopt bicycle lanes, and usage of electric cars. In addition to booster charging cars from new phases of PV systems.
extraction_rationale: Specific low-carbon transport planning action with electric mobility and PV charging.

policy_statement: Implement Al-Qurna Priority Action #3, Solar PV for Heritage Sites, using off-grid PV with lithium batteries at Kings Valley, the mountain and Hatshepsut temple.
source_quote:
Implementation plan

Component 1: The plan is to develop solar PV units off-grid with lithium batteries to serve the electricity situation in the Kings Valley and the mountain and Hatshepsut temple.

Every 1kW of solar PV takes up 8 m 2 . Thus, to serve the 160kW electricity demand for Upper area of the mountain, an area of 1,280 m 2 would be needed.
extraction_rationale: Named priority action with renewable-energy technology, sites and capacity assumptions.

policy_statement: Implement Al-Qurna Priority Action #4, Management of Agriculture Waste, through machinery, leasing and recycling of agricultural waste to avoid burning and reduce emissions.
source_quote:
Implementation plan

Phase 1: Component 1: Estimate the needs and requirements of the west side.

Start with limited numbers of tractors, trailers, shredder machines and trucks. Exact number needed to cover a vast range of farms in Al-Qurna:

10 Tractors, 10 shredder machines, 20 Trailers.
extraction_rationale: Named priority action with specified machinery and agriculture-waste recycling measures.

policy_statement: Implement Al-Qurna Priority Action #5, the Environmental Public Awareness Unit, to reduce residential electricity consumption by 15%.
source_quote:
With the success of the awareness project, we assumed a reduction of 15% in residential buildings.

In 2015, the population of the city of Luxor is equal to 586,025 persons, consuming 690,697 MWh/year of electricity.
extraction_rationale: Named priority action with quantified energy-reduction assumption.

policy_statement: Implement Al-Qurna Priority Action #6, Waterfront Aesthetics, to safeguard the green waterfront, remove encroachments, rationalize mountain lighting and raise environmental awareness.
source_quote:
Component 1 : Investing on what is called Mehleb committee, named after the ex-prime-minister commissioned by H.E. President to clear all violations along the River Nile, coordination among concerned stakeholders. The committee is an essential need to confront the current rapid pace of uncontrolled development consuming the green belt and casting a grey ugly shadow in what used to a spectacular heritage panoramic view characterising Luxor.

Component 2: An awareness campaign is also needed to raise the awareness of the importance of preserving the aesthetics and environmental balance of the West Bank waterfront among all stakeholders: SCA, Localities & Luxor Governorate, Local Community & private investors in tourism sector, mainly hotels and hotel chains.
extraction_rationale: Named action using green-belt protection and lighting rationalization; climate relevance is indirect because heritage/aesthetics are also central.

policy_statement: Develop the Al-Qurna integrated master plan by selecting a management team, issuing TOR/RFP, hiring a consultant, holding workshops and declaring agreed plan components.
source_quote:
Component 1 : Select and formulate the integrated master plan development management team (committee) and its coordinator,

Component 2: Develop the TOR and release the RFP and select the winning bidder/ consultant or consultancy,

- Component 3: Follow up master plan development process including organising 2 workshops,
- Component 4: Hold the workshops and the national meeting to declare the agreed upon components of the developed integrated master plan to facilitate its implementation and all cooperation and coordination necessary to fulfil that.
extraction_rationale: Named mid-term SECAP project fiche with concrete planning steps; climate relevance is indirect because it is an integrated sustainable development planning tool.

policy_statement: Achieve aggregate community GHG reductions of 15% by 2020, 51% by 2035, and 71% by 2050 relative to the 2016 base year through the plan's priority climate actions.
source_quote: At the culmination of the climate planning process, stakeholders identified nineteen priority climate actions that in the aggregate could achieve GHG reductions of 15% by 2020, 51% by 2035, and 71% by 2050 relative to the 2016 base year. As shown in the table on the following page, priority actions were quantified by both their CO 2 abatement potential, how cost effective they were at abating emissions, and their alignment and potential beneficial impact on goals in the Memphis 3.0 Comprehensive Plan.
extraction_rationale: Quantified communitywide greenhouse gas reduction pathway in the climate action plan.

policy_statement: Set local government operations GHG reduction targets for buildings and fleet vehicles: buildings 20% by 2020, 55% by 2035, and 80% by 2050; fleet vehicles 15% by 2020, 45% by 2035, and 80% by 2050.
source_quote: Memphis and Shelby County should set GHG reduction targets that exceed the community-wide targets (see Chapter 1). Proposed reduction targets for both City and County government operations are as follows: Year 2020 Buildings 20% Fleet Vehicles 15%; 2035 Buildings 55% Fleet Vehicles 45%; 2050 Buildings 80% Fleet Vehicles 80%.
extraction_rationale: Quantified emissions-reduction targets for local government buildings and fleets.

policy_statement: Reduce Namibia's GHG emissions by approximately 21.996 MtCO2e in 2030, a 91% reduction against the BAU scenario of 24.167 MtCO2e.
source_quote: In  the  BAU  scenario,  overall  GHG  emissions  in  2030  are  expected  to  rise  by  up  to  24.167  MtCO2e.  The estimated emissions reduction under the NDC scenario will be approximately 21.996 MtCO2e in 2030 (91% reduction of which 78.7% is from the AFOLU) (Table 2.4). The total mitigation potential is estimated at around 21.996 MtCO2e in 2030 compared to BAU emissions in the same year of 24.167 MtCO2e (Figure 2.1). According to the analysis, mitigation measures identified within the  AFOLU sector account for the highest proportion (approximately 79%) (Table 2.4) compared to other sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is the national quantified NDC mitigation outcome for 2030 against BAU; it is a clear target supported by sectoral measures.

policy_statement: Under NDP5, achieve a 30% greenhouse-gas emissions reduction against the BAU projection by 2022 and monitor/report it annually under Paris Agreement rules.
source_quote: For the first time in a National Development Plan (NDP5), Namibia included an intermediate emissions reduction target (Greenhouse gas emissions 30% reduction against Business As Usual projection, by 2022). This target is a carbon budget which the country can 'spend' in diverse ways by allocating emission rights and commitments among those sectors most responsible for greenhouse gas emissions. The target is an important signal for private stakeholders and potential investors, giving them the incentive to find mitigation opportunities. NDP5 targets 10 are subject to domestic monitoring and annual reporting: The Government of Namibia will necessarily follow an emission monitoring and reporting system based on the rules of the Paris Agreement (which were agreed at COP24).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified intermediate emissions-reduction target with a monitoring/reporting mechanism; it is included as a climate policy even though it predates the NDC update.

policy_statement: Implement Law 10/91 and related rules to reduce heat consumption in new and restructured residential and service buildings.

policy_statement: Use carbon-tax revenues for compensation and subsidies for emissions reduction, energy efficiency and renewable energy.
source_quote: This section addresses measures involving sectors which were not directly discussed in the preceding sections. Law 448/98 , which introduced the carbon tax, mentioned that the Government would be able to draw on a portion of the resulting revenues for use as compensation for the measures taken in the different sectors and as subsidies for the reduction of emissions, for the promotion of energy efficiency and for the development of renewable sources. policy_statement: Install thermal or catalytic devices for adipic-acid N2O emissions through a voluntary agreement.
source_quote: ## Reduction of N2O emissions from the production of adipic acid and nitric acid These two interventions can result in significant reductions in the emissions from industrial processes, with extremely limited reduction costs. In the case of adipic acid, the planned course of action calls for the adoption in Italy of the devices (thermal or catalytic) already used in the other European countries for the treatment of effluent gases. The measure referred to consists of a voluntary agreement with the only enterprise involved.
section_header: ## Reduction of N2O emissions from the production of adipic acid and nitric acid

section_header: ## Reduction of N2O emissions from the production of adipic acid and nitric acid
extraction_rationale: Specific N2O abatement technology and voluntary agreement.

policy_statement: Promote organic agriculture expansion, assuming 30% lower energy use than traditional agriculture.
source_quote: Assuming that the specific level of energy consumption of organic agriculture is 30% lower than that of traditional agriculture, a projection through 2010 of current growth trends in the sector shows that the emissions avoided could total 0.337 Mt CO2. This figure could be reduced to 0.28 Mt CO2, taking into account the possible saturation of the sector, as well as the fact that the lower level of energy consumption in the production of fertilisers is considered under another item of the emissions inventory.
extraction_rationale: Agricultural practice shift with quantified energy and CO2 effects.

policy_statement: Cover liquid animal-waste tanks and convey biogas to combustion or cogeneration plants to reduce methane emissions.
source_quote: ## Emissions of methane from manure management The proposed initiative involves covering the holding tanks used to store liquid animal waste and then conveying the resulting biogas to combustion or cogeneration plants. The primary focus of the activities would be pigs (between 10% and 40% of the animals) and, to a relatively limited degree, cattle, with a reduction in methane emissions of between 7 and 39 kt of methane per year, at an overall cost of from 6.2 to 33.2 million Euro per year.
section_header: ## Emissions of methane from manure management
extraction_rationale: Specific manure methane-abatement and biogas measure with cost and reduction estimates.

policy_statement: Apply IPPC licensing based on best available technology to large poultry and pig farms, with possible Rural Development Plan incentives for existing facilities.
source_quote: Another measure oriented towards this same objective is Directive 96/61/EC (Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control, or IPPC), which calls for the introduction of licensing processes based on the adoption of the best possible technology available for poultry farms with more than 40,000 birds and pig farms with more than 2,000 animals (heavier than 30 kg) or 750 sows. In terms of structural initiatives for existing facilities, financial incentives could be drawn from within the Rural Development Plans (PSR) financed by the FEOGA.
section_header: ## Emissions of methane from manure management
extraction_rationale: Binding licensing/BAT requirement and possible incentives for livestock emissions control.

We have assumed that, on the quantity of recycled aluminium will grow, between now and the year 2010, up to approximately 80% of the total consumption of this metal.
extraction_rationale: Material recycling target with explicit PFC and energy benefits.

The European industry has voluntarily agreed to limit its emissions in 2010 to a figure 10% lower than 1995 levels.
extraction_rationale: Industrial F-gas abatement measure with quantified industry target.

These initiatives shall be promoted under the European framework-directive currently up for discussion.
extraction_rationale: Specific F-gas leakage reduction measure.
