policy_statement: By 30 April 2003, present a detailed 2004-2006 plan for national carbon-removal activities using dedicated public resources.
source_quote: Further emission reductions can be achieved through afforestation and reforestation activities, management of forest resources, farmlands and grazing lands and revegetation according to point G of Table 6 annexed this document. 7.1 Before 30 April 2003, the Ministry of the Environment and Territory, in agreement with the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies and with the Conference of State-Regions, presents to this Committee the detailed plan referring to the first three-year period 2004-2006, for the realization of the national activities specified in Table 6 in the frame of public resources purposely devoted.
section_header: ## D E C R E E S
extraction_rationale: Dated planning and public-resource commitment for land carbon removals.

policy_statement: By 30 July 2003, identify regulations enabling certification of human-induced natural reforestation from 1990-2012.
source_quote: 7.2 Before 30 July 2003, the Ministry of the Environment and Defence of the Territory, in agreement with the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies, takes measures to identify among the regional, national and international provisions in force in Italy from 1990 to date, all regulations contemplating the defence of the Italian forest stand, with the aim of certifying 'natural reforestation' activities carried out on the national territory in the period 1990-2012, as a direct consequence of human activities and, consequently, eligible to the purpose of achieving the emission reduction objective established by law 120/2002.
section_header: ## D E C R E E S
extraction_rationale: Dated legal review to certify forest carbon removals.

policy_statement: By 31 May 2005, prepare the National Forestry Inventory on Carbon and other carbon reservoirs.
source_quote: 7.3 Before 31 May 2005 the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies, in agreement with the Ministry of the Environment and Territory, prepares the National Forestry Inventory on Carbon and other Carbon Reservoirs in order to start the procedure to revise the limit of use of the credits deriving from the mana Revised guidelines for national policies and measures regarding the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (Law 120/2002)
section_header: ## D E C R E E S
extraction_rationale: Dated inventory commitment for carbon accounting.

policy_statement: By 31 December 2006, prepare the National Register of agro-forestry carbon reservoirs for certification of 2008-2012 carbon flows.
source_quote: 7.4 Before 31 December 2006, the Ministry of Environment and Territory, in agreement with the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies, prepares the National Register of agro-forestry carbon reservoirs, in order to certify the carbon flows deriving from the sectors of afforestation, reforestation, deforestation, forest management, management of farmlands and grazing lands and revegetation from 2008 to 2012.
section_header: ## D E C R E E S
extraction_rationale: Dated institutional commitment for land-sector carbon certification.

policy_statement: From 2003, include a section on the National Action Plan in the annual Economic and Financial Planning Document.
source_quote: As from 2003, in arranging the yearly Document of Economic and Financial Planning (DPEF), the Ministry of Economics and Finance will include a section devoted to this Plan, including the necessary tools for reaching the established objectives.
section_header: ## D E C R E E S
extraction_rationale: Planning and budget integration requirement for climate plan implementation.

policy_statement: Adopt sea-level-rise adaptation measures to address negative effects of relative sea-level rise in Italy.
source_quote: Such episodes, in fact, have recently reached alarming levels and rates due to effective subsidence phenomena and, above all, to meteorological and climate events (prevalence of southerly winds). Among the others, the following measures should be adopted to thwart the negative effects of the relative sea level rise in Italy, such as: Channelling and pumping works with draining pumps of depressed areas following reclamation works;
extraction_rationale: Adaptation package followed by numbered measures.

parent_statement: Sea-level-rise adaptation measures
policy_statement: Implement channelling and pumping works with draining pumps for depressed reclaimed areas.
source_quote: Among the others, the following measures should be adopted to thwart the negative effects of the relative sea level rise in Italy, such as: Channelling and pumping works with draining pumps of depressed areas following reclamation works;
extraction_rationale: Specific flood/sea-level adaptation infrastructure.

parent_statement: Sea-level-rise adaptation measures
policy_statement: Dismantle gas-hydrocarbon and water wells to address subsidence-related sea-level vulnerability.
source_quote: A study aimed at analysing the changes (level, power, consumption etc.) performed over time in the plants of many Italian plains, is strongly suggested. ## 6.3.2.2 Dismantling of wells for gas-hydrocarbons and water Remarkable subsidence phenomena (nearly 10cm/year) occurred between the 60s and the 80s in the area between Cesenatico and Ravenna causing the closing of methane-producing and water-exploiting wells. The response to these 'adaptation measures' was almost immediate, and subsidence rates reverted to more acceptable mm/year values.
section_header: ## 6.3.2.2 Dismantling of wells for gas-hydrocarbons and water
extraction_rationale: Specific subsidence adaptation measure.

parent_statement: Sea-level-rise adaptation measures
policy_statement: Use sand feeding to rebuild eroded coastal sand mantles.
source_quote: ## 6.3.2.3 Sand feeding Following to coastal erosion caused by different factors, hundred billion sums have been spent every year to rebuild the sand mantle for mere tourist purposes. 6 Total cost associated with climate change impacts is considered, in literature, as the total of adaptation costs and residual damage.
extraction_rationale: Specific coastal erosion response; text notes tourism motivation as well.

parent_statement: Sea-level-rise adaptation measures
policy_statement: Regulate or close water pumping plants to manage saline wedge intrusion in coastal aquifers.
source_quote: ## 6.3.2.4 Saline wedge In the coastal areas, the balance that has formed between fresh-water and salt-water aquifers creates an unstable 'system' due to several reasons. It is clear that a (negative) variation in the balance between fresh-water and salt-water aquifers may cause an increase in sea base level, and that a decrease in fresh-water aquifers (on account of overexploitation) may cause the breaking of such balance.
extraction_rationale: Water-management adaptation for saline intrusion.

policy_statement: Implement the MOSE plan in Venice to keep down maximum peak levels during high-water episodes.
source_quote: The implementation of the Mose plan in Venice can be considered as one of the most representative efforts ever made to face the sea-rise issue. It should answer the purpose of 'keeping down' maximum peak levels during high water episodes. Such episodes, in fact, have recently reached alarming levels and rates due to effective subsidence phenomena and, above all, to meteorological and climate events (prevalence of southerly winds).
extraction_rationale: Named sea-level/high-water adaptation infrastructure.

policy_statement: Implement the National Action Plan to Combat Desertification, including regional and basin-authority programmes for prevention, mitigation and adaptation.
source_quote: The Regions and the Basin Authorities have been sided by a working group to set up the guidelines and summarise the different proposals. Ten Regions and eleven Basin Authorities covering, in total, 87% of the national territory, have presented their programmes to the National Committee to Combat Desertification. The scope of the Plan has been successively enlarged to non-arid zones affected by territorial degradation phenomena, even if not associated to climate change factors.
extraction_rationale: Named national adaptation plan for desertification hazard.

policy_statement: Adopt agricultural adaptation actions to counter undesired climate-change effects in agriculture.
source_quote: ## 6.3.4 Agriculture The Italian actions aimed at thwarting the undesired effects of climate change in the agricultural sector follow the indications provided in the Agenda 21 of the United Nations. They consist in:
extraction_rationale: Adaptation action package followed by sub-actions.

parent_statement: Agricultural adaptation actions
policy_statement: Arrange territorial and land-use planning that considers present and expected global changes.
source_quote: They consist in: the arrangement of an attentive territorial and landuse planning according to a multifunctional view, taking into consideration both present and expected global changes;
extraction_rationale: Specific agricultural adaptation planning action.

parent_statement: Agricultural adaptation actions
policy_statement: Create diversified agricultural production compatible with local territory and climate region.
source_quote: the arrangement of an attentive territorial and landuse planning according to a multifunctional view, taking into consideration both present and expected global changes; the creation of diversified agricultural productions compatible with local territorial peculiarities and with the climatic region where the farmland is to be established;
extraction_rationale: Specific agricultural diversification adaptation action.

parent_statement: Agricultural adaptation actions
policy_statement: Protect and conserve biological and ecological diversity and genetic, vegetable and animal resources.
source_quote: the creation of diversified agricultural productions compatible with local territorial peculiarities and with the climatic region where the farmland is to be established; protection and conservation of biological and ecological diversity and existing genetic heredity in terms of genetic, vegetable and animal resources;
extraction_rationale: Nature-based agricultural resilience measure.

parent_statement: Agricultural adaptation actions
policy_statement: Use energy efficiently in agricultural and food-production practices.
source_quote: protection and conservation of biological and ecological diversity and existing genetic heredity in terms of genetic, vegetable and animal resources; efficient energy use in agricultural and food-production practices;
extraction_rationale: Specific resource-efficiency action in adaptation package.

parent_statement: Agricultural adaptation actions
policy_statement: Plan surface and aquifer water resources, enhance water accumulation and storage, remove water pollutants and reduce water misuse.
source_quote: attentive planning of surface and aquifer water resources compatible with agricultural, human and industrial requirements, with particular reference to: a) enhancement of infrastructures for water accumulation and storage; b) removal of discharges and pollutants that may contaminate water resources;
extraction_rationale: Specific water-resource adaptation package.

policy_statement: Implement forest adaptation measures to protect Italian forests from degradation, desertification and climate disturbances.
source_quote: ## 6.3.5 Forests The actions to protect the Italian forests also contribute to prevent degradation and desertification phenomena. The following measures need particular attention:
extraction_rationale: Forest adaptation package followed by sub-actions.

parent_statement: Forest adaptation measures
policy_statement: Increase specific and structural forest biodiversity to improve resistance and resilience to disturbances.
source_quote: The following measures need particular attention: the increase of specific and structural forest biodiversity improving resistance and resilience to disturbances. This measure would enable forests to adapt at the ever-changing climate conditions ensuring tree coverage, both in terms of space and time, even if this would imply the formation of different tree species;
extraction_rationale: Ecosystem-based adaptation explicitly improving resilience.

parent_statement: Forest adaptation measures
policy_statement: Establish new poly-specific forest plantations on abandoned lands.
source_quote: the establishment of new poly-specific forest plants on abandoned lands;
extraction_rationale: Specific ecosystem-based forest expansion action.

parent_statement: Forest adaptation measures
policy_statement: Create wooded areas in agro-industrial landscapes and urban areas.
source_quote: the creation of wooded areas in agro-industrial landscapes and urban areas;
extraction_rationale: Specific greening action under forest adaptation package.

parent_statement: Forest adaptation measures
policy_statement: Implement efficient fire-prevention and extinction policies.
source_quote: the implementation of efficient fire-prevention and extinction policies.
extraction_rationale: Specific fire hazard-management adaptation action.

policy_statement: Qatar intends to reduce its GHG emissions by 25% by 2030 relative to the business-as-usual baseline.
source_quote: This current communication reflects an enhanced ambition by the State of Qatar towards reducing its overall emissions in response to the guidance set forth in Article 4.4 of the Paris Agreement. Qatar intends to reduce 25% of its GHG emissions by the year 2030, relative to baseline scenario {BusinessAs-Usual (BAU)}.
extraction_rationale: This is the central NDC mitigation target and contains a quantified emissions reduction commitment and deadline.

policy_statement: Qatar has implemented oil and gas emissions-reduction projects including the Al Shaheen flare reduction project, Jetty boil-off gas recovery project, and the Al-Shaheen Oil Field Gas Recovery and Utilization CDM project.
source_quote: The Al Shaheen flare reduction project (one of the world's largest) and the Jetty boil-off gas recovery project have laid solid foundations towards emission reduction. The Al-Shaheen Oil Field Gas Recovery and Utilization Project has been registered as a Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) project since 2007 for 21 years within the framework of the Kyoto Protocol. The project received approval from the UNFCCC for the seven-year crediting period from 2014 to 2021, and it is expected to abate approximately 1.2 million tons of CO2 each year during this period.
extraction_rationale: These are named oil and gas emissions-reduction projects, including a CDM project with quantified annual CO2 abatement. The action is partly historical, but it is presented in the NDC as part of Qatar's mitigation-measure portfolio.

policy_statement: Qatar Petroleum is committed to zero routine flaring by 2030 and minimizing technically feasible non-routine flaring.
source_quote: The national oil company, Qatar Petroleum (QP), is committed to zero routine flaring by 2030, with a long-term goal to reduce flaring in onshore facilities to the absolute minimum. Technically feasible non-routine flaring is also covered.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear mitigation commitment with a 2030 deadline and a specific flaring-reduction mechanism.

policy_statement: Qatar will use carbon capture and storage, including a 2.2 MTPA Ras Laffan facility and CCS for new LNG facilities, to reduce oil and gas sector GHG emissions.
source_quote: Carbon capture storage (CCS) will be another pivotal measure for reducing the GHG emissions from the sector. Qatar commissioned the largest CO2 recovery and sequestration facility in the MENA region at Ras Laffan in 2019 with a design capacity of 2.2 MTPA of CO2 capture and storage. CCS is included for new LNG facilities and concepts, for remaining LNG facilities will be developed and implemented considering the economic, safety and environmental concerns.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific mitigation technology deployment commitment with quantified capture/storage capacity and planned extension to LNG facilities.

policy_statement: Qatar Petroleum will reduce methane emissions through guiding principles, leak detection and repair, and a planned integrated fugitive methane monitoring and repair program across all assets.
source_quote: QP signed a set of Guiding Principles on 22 March 2018 that aim to reduce methane emissions across the natural gas value chain stretching from production to the final consumer. In 2019, Qatar Petroleum introduced the smart leak detection and repair program (LDAR) in all upstream and downstream facilities of the oil & gas industry. Qatar further plans to move towards a fully integrated fugitive methane monitoring and repair program across all assets.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific methane mitigation policy package, including a named LDAR program and a planned monitoring and repair program.

policy_statement: Qatar will implement oil and gas energy-efficiency projects by 2025, including turbine and boiler optimization, fuel gas and steam balancing, HRSG reliability, waste heat recovery, and excess fuel/off-gas recycling.
source_quote: Qatar is enhancing energy efficiency in the oil & gas sector as a key measure to reduce GHG emissions. The energy efficiency program includes several projects that are allocated in upstream facilities as well as gas-to-liquid and downstream facilities. Amongst the variety of measures in energy efficiency, certain initiatives are aimed to be implemented by 2025, e.g., seasonal optimization of gas turbine generators and boilers, improved measurement / balancing for fuel gas / steam, and improved reliability of heat recovery steam generator (HRSGs).
extraction_rationale: This is a named sectoral energy-efficiency program with specific interventions and an implementation deadline. GHG reduction is explicitly stated, but the primary mechanism is efficiency.

policy_statement: Qatar plans to optimize and share electrical generation capacity across upstream and GTL facilities to reduce gas consumption and GHG emissions.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to efficiently utilize its power plant capacities by usage in other upstream facilities or feed-in from GTL (gas-to-liquid) facilities to its utility distribution / transmission grid. Electrical generation capacity shall be shared and optimized across all upstream facilities. This would allow more efficient dispatch of generating capacity and keep the units closer to their most efficient operating levels, thereby reducing gas consumption and GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational efficiency commitment in the oil and gas sector, explicitly linked to reducing gas consumption and GHG emissions.

policy_statement: Qatar is introducing its first 800 MW solar power plant and aims to expand renewable energy as a key driver of ecological and commercial benefits.
source_quote: Nevertheless, recently Qatar has made significant progress in reducing the emissions from the power & water sector, by introducing its first 800 MW solar power plant, which shall be operational soon. It is the goal of the State of Qatar to expand these efforts and transform renewable energy into a key driver for ecological and commercial benefits.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable-energy deployment commitment with a quantified plant capacity and a stated expansion goal.

policy_statement: Qatar will continue and expand the Tarsheed program to reduce per-capita electricity and water consumption, improve demand-side energy efficiency, and support rooftop solar generation.
source_quote: The National Program for Conservative & Efficient use of Water & Electricity (Tarsheed) has been successful in generating a lasting awareness over the issue of water and energy wastage, especially among the youth, and in reducing consumption of electricity & water per capita. It has ambitious aims for further reductions. Led by Qatar Foundation, Education City and the Qatar Green Building Council, efforts are being made to enhance the demand-side energy efficiency, energy savings, and local energy generation through rooftops solar panels.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national conservation program with specific resource-efficiency objectives and rooftop solar actions; the future scale of reductions is not quantified.

policy_statement: Qatar is systematically deploying energy labeling and equipment specification standards to reduce energy intensity, electricity consumption, and household and SME GHG emissions.
source_quote: Energy efficiency measures such as district cooling and energy labeling for all electronic devices are systematically being deployed and play a growing role in the national economic diversification strategy by reducing energy intensity and the need for energy subsidies, while also mitigating the overall GHG emissions of households and small & medium enterprises. Qatar has implemented several specification improvement standards for electrical and electronic equipment such as air conditioners resulting in significant savings in electricity consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific efficiency standards and labeling policy. It explicitly mentions GHG mitigation, but the primary mechanism is energy-efficiency improvement.

policy_statement: Qatar is phasing out incandescent lamps and adopting energy-efficient lighting to conserve energy and reduce GHG emissions.
source_quote: The initiative to phase out incandescent lamps and adoption of Energy Efficient lighting has contributed in a major way for conservation of Energy and thereby GHG emissions reduction in the State of Qatar. Qatar is considered a pioneer in the field of district cooling (DC).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific lighting technology transition policy tied to energy conservation and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Qatar is using district cooling to deliver large-scale centralized cooling and save energy consumption and infrastructure.
source_quote: Qatar is considered a pioneer in the field of district cooling (DC). District cooling relies on largescale centralized cooling that provides a wide spectrum of savings in energy consumption and infrastructure. It consequently reduces impact on the environment.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific cooling infrastructure intervention with explicit energy and infrastructure savings.

policy_statement: Qatar is upgrading sewage treatment plants to produce treated effluent for landscaping, irrigation, district cooling, construction, and other uses.
source_quote: The DC system operations are essentially linked to the electricity and water consumption. The continuous improvements in both electricity and water management practices substantially contribute to the environmental sustainability of the receiving housing and public buildings. Lastly, Qatar has continuously strived to upgrade its sewage treatment plants to produce treated effluents suitable for purposes such as landscaping, fodder crops irrigation, district cooling, construction industry use, etc.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water-reuse infrastructure intervention through sewage treatment plant upgrades.

policy_statement: Qatar has developed public transport infrastructure through the Doha Metro and Lusail Tram to reduce transport emissions.
source_quote: The transportation sector in Qatar has been earmarked for rapid modernization. The Doha Metro and Lusail Tram are major milestones in the development of public transportation and subsequent reduction of emissions from this sector. The level 3 accreditation status for Hamad International Airport is another major initiative towards sustainability.
extraction_rationale: The Doha Metro and Lusail Tram are named public transport interventions explicitly linked to reducing transport emissions.

policy_statement: Qatar is electrifying its public transport system and installing EV charging infrastructure across the country.
source_quote: The Doha Metro and Lusail Tram are major milestones in the development of public transportation and subsequent reduction of emissions from this sector. The level 3 accreditation status for Hamad International Airport is another major initiative towards sustainability. The country has also taken significant strides to adopt electrification of on-road vehicles by committing to electrify its public transport system and investing in installation of charging infrastructure across the country.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport electrification commitment supported by charging infrastructure deployment and explicitly linked to emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Qatar will promote a shift from internal-combustion vehicles to electric vehicles and provide EV charging infrastructure to reduce transport-sector GHG emissions.
source_quote: Transition from ICE vehicles to EV and providing necessary infrastructure for EV chargers will contribute in a major way for GHG reduction and thereby NDC goals. Electrification has also been adopted in port operations e.g. reducing emissions at Hamad port using electric tractors. Going forward, gradual adoption of Euro 6 emission standards for vehicles and promoting a shift towards electric vehicles for private use shall constitute key initiatives to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport decarbonization policy using EV adoption and charging infrastructure; it explicitly targets GHG and transport emissions.

policy_statement: Qatar will gradually adopt Euro 6 vehicle emission standards.
source_quote: Transition from ICE vehicles to EV and providing necessary infrastructure for EV chargers will contribute in a major way for GHG reduction and thereby NDC goals. Electrification has also been adopted in port operations e.g. reducing emissions at Hamad port using electric tractors. Going forward, gradual adoption of Euro 6 emission standards for vehicles and promoting a shift towards electric vehicles for private use shall constitute key initiatives to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory vehicle-emissions standard commitment. Although Euro 6 also targets air pollutants, the text frames it as a transport emissions-reduction initiative.

policy_statement: Qatar is reducing port-operation emissions at Hamad Port through electric tractors.
source_quote: Transition from ICE vehicles to EV and providing necessary infrastructure for EV chargers will contribute in a major way for GHG reduction and thereby NDC goals. Electrification has also been adopted in port operations e.g. reducing emissions at Hamad port using electric tractors. Going forward, gradual adoption of Euro 6 emission standards for vehicles and promoting a shift towards electric vehicles for private use shall constitute key initiatives to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific electrification intervention in port operations, explicitly framed as emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Qatar is adopting Global Sustainability Assessment System standards and higher sustainability standards for hotels and buildings.
source_quote: Qatar has been transforming its building standards towards higher sustainability levels through the adoption of the Global Sustainability Assessment System (GSAS) standards. The number of projects registered for GSAS certifications has been rapidly increasing thereby facilitating the transition towards green buildings. The Qatar Green Building Council has been advising hotels on higher environmental standards for energy and water savings, and has certified an increasing number of hotels, in line with the new hotel classification system implemented by the Qatar Tourism Authority (QTA) which has set new and higher sustainability standard.
extraction_rationale: This is a building standards and certification policy with specific named standards and resource savings outcomes.

policy_statement: Hamad International Airport's second expansion terminal will achieve a 4-star GSAS rating, LEED Silver certification, and building-wide energy-efficiency measures.
source_quote: In its plans for the second expansion phase, the terminal building will be the first airport in the MENA region to achieve a 4-star Global Sustainability Assessment System (GSAS) rating, which is the first performance-based system in the MENA region, developed for rating the green buildings and infrastructures. The terminal will also be a LEED Silver certified building with innovative measures of energy efficiency across the entire building.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure sustainability commitment with named certification levels and energy-efficiency measures.

policy_statement: Qatar plans to promote decentralized renewable energy production and energy-efficient consumption in buildings.
source_quote: A steadily growing number of projects to install solar panels on residential buildings are being undertaken by the private sector. Qatar plans to promote decentralized renewable energy production and use in buildings while also making more efficient their energy consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific building-sector policy combining rooftop solar promotion and energy-efficiency improvements.

policy_statement: Qatar is developing Lusail City as a smart and sustainable city with centralized water, cooling, waste, and transport systems and solar energy production.
source_quote: Qatar plans to promote decentralized renewable energy production and use in buildings while also making more efficient their energy consumption. The ongoing development of Lusail city is Qatar's main initiative concerning smart and sustainable cities with centralized water, cooling, waste, and transport systems as well as solar energy production.
extraction_rationale: This is a named sustainable urban development initiative with specific infrastructure systems and solar energy production.

policy_statement: Qatar is implementing construction waste recycling and reuse and plans to explore battery-powered generators for construction activities.
source_quote: The ongoing development of Lusail city is Qatar's main initiative concerning smart and sustainable cities with centralized water, cooling, waste, and transport systems as well as solar energy production. Qatar has been making a steady progress towards attaining circular economy in the construction sector by implementing recycling and re-using construction waste and the government further plans to explore the use of environment friendly battery-powered generators for construction activities.
extraction_rationale: This is a circular-economy and cleaner construction equipment policy with specific waste and technology interventions.

policy_statement: QEERI has released the Qatar Solar Atlas and supports research to accelerate solar energy use in Qatar.
source_quote: Similar research activities are also conducted at Hamad Bin Khalifa University & its affiliated research institute, Qatar Environment and Energy Research Institute (QEERI), has released the first Qatar Solar Atlas, a tool that quantifies the country's solar resource and geographical distribution as a first step towards accelerating the use of more solar energy across the country. In addition, the recent Air Quality Index and Inhalable Particulates Index to provide the local population with information on gas and particulate emissions in Qatar. Partnered efforts, with international research centers, are being made to develop economic ways of harnessing solar energy through both fundamental and applied research on materials.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate-relevant R&D intervention supporting renewable-energy deployment; it is enabling rather than a direct emissions regulation.

policy_statement: The Qatar National Research Fund is funding research for an efficient national-scale carbon management system.
source_quote: The Qatar Research, Development and Innovation Council (QRDI) focuses on key topics of sustainability in Qatar's energy sector and in management of environmental, food and water resources. Meanwhile, the Qatar National Research Fund (QNRF) is funding research for an efficient carbon management system at the national scale.
extraction_rationale: This is a committed research funding action for carbon management, making it both climate-relevant and a financial instrument.

policy_statement: The Ministry of Education and Higher Education operates Eco School programs and has established a sustainable development committee to address climate change through education.
source_quote: Since 1994, the Ministry of Education and Higher Education has introduced the 'Eco School programs' initiative which promotes environmental education and awareness in primary and secondary levels. This is realized through parts of the curriculum covering climate change in combination with extracurricular activities. Building upon this legacy, the Ministry has also established a committee for sustainable development to enhance all activities in this sphere and address climate change through education.
extraction_rationale: This is a named climate education program and institutional committee. It is concrete, though its climate effect is indirect and behavioral.

policy_statement: Qatar plans to enhance teacher training on climate change topics to support sustainability education and long-term behavioral change.
source_quote: On a more applied level, the state of Qatar is eager to foster climate change education throughout the daily routines of educational institutions. This is illustrated by the plan for enhancing teachers' training on climate change topics in order to enable educators to present the topics of sustainability and environmental development in an appealing manner to students, and to foster behavioral changes in the long-term.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planned capacity-building intervention for climate education. Its implementation details are somewhat vague.

policy_statement: Major university campuses in Qatar use rooftop solar panels and policies to reduce energy consumption.
source_quote: Also, all major university campuses in Qatar feature solar panels on building rooftops and policies to reduce energy consumption. Qatar Foundation (QF) is developing green campus and housing facilities which have a direct impact on the ecological footprint of facilities and additionally increases awareness and consciousness of students.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete campus-level renewable energy and energy efficiency policy.

policy_statement: Qatar Foundation is developing green campus and housing facilities and campaigns to reduce single-use plastics and support annual collection campaigns.
source_quote: Qatar Foundation (QF) is developing green campus and housing facilities which have a direct impact on the ecological footprint of facilities and additionally increases awareness and consciousness of students. Further projects include initiatives such as awareness campaigns advocating for banning single-use plastics in society and annual collection campaigns. By means of initiatives like these, the State of Qatar is developing a generation that is aware of climate change and capable of limiting its own carbon footprint and to develop sustainable countermeasures.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional sustainability initiative involving green facilities and waste-related campaigns. The climate link is partly educational and behavioral.

policy_statement: Education City operates a tram across 24 stations and 11.5 km using hybrid energy storage.
source_quote: Also, the Education City in QF, which is an extensive campus with a world class national library, several branches of leading international universities, schools and research centers, has been developing a strategy to implement solutions for a more sustainable educational complex. The Education City tram, for instance, now connects 24 designated tram stations across 11.5 km and runs on hybrid energy storage (HES).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific low-carbon campus transport intervention with quantified route/station information and a named energy-storage technology.

policy_statement: Qatar's tourism strategy promotes sustainable tourism, including eco-resorts, to reduce dependence on hydrocarbon resources for economic growth.
source_quote: The development of the country's first eco-resorts and major events like the FIFA World Cup 2022 and the Asian Games 2030 are set to further enhance the touristic appeal of the country while driving its socio-economic growth in a sustainable manner. Qatar's tourism strategy promotes sustainable tourism and aims to reduce dependence on hydrocarbon resources for economic growth.
extraction_rationale: This is a named sector strategy with specific eco-resort development and economic diversification goals. Its climate relevance is indirect because the main aim is tourism and diversification.

policy_statement: Qatar aims to reduce per-capita power and water consumption and use less energy-intensive technologies throughout the water value chain.
source_quote: Qatar depends mostly on seawater desalination for urban water supply, often using energy-intensive technologies. In the future, it is essential to reduce the consumption of both power and water per capita and use less energy-intensive technologies throughout the entire value stream.
extraction_rationale: This is a resource-efficiency commitment for water and energy use, though the exact reduction target is not quantified.

policy_statement: Qatar is implementing water-conservation regulation and measures including high-consumption customer messages, aerator retrofits in government facilities, and switching parks to treated sewage effluent irrigation.
source_quote: Besides the implementation of a new and ambitious water conservation regulation, several other measures have been started, e.g., increasing awareness via messages to residential customers with high consumption, retrofitting and replacing aerators in governmental facilities and switching to treated sewage effluent (TSE) for irrigation in parks. Additionally, savings are increasingly made by using recycled water in district cooling, the construction industry, and for a growing number of other usages.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory and operational water conservation policy with specific interventions.

policy_statement: Qatar is using treated sewage effluent as a significant water-management adaptation measure, with 194 million cubic meters of TSE in 2015 amounting to about 98.2% of total wastewater.
source_quote: Efficient water management is a key adaptation measure. Therefore, Qatar has also invested significantly in this field. As a result, treated sewage effluent (TSE) volume in 2015 amounted to 194 million cubic meters or around 98.2% of total wastewater.
extraction_rationale: This is a water reuse and wastewater management intervention explicitly described as an adaptation measure and supported by quantified reuse volumes.

policy_statement: Qatar has developed a National Water Policy, draft National Water Law and executive by-law, and a draft law regulating groundwater well drilling.
source_quote: Moreover, as part of the development of Qatar's Water Plan and Strategy, the National Water Policy was developed as the draft of the National Water Law and its executive by-law have been finalized. Furthermore, a draft law to regulate groundwater wells drilling has been completed.
extraction_rationale: This is a water governance and regulatory policy package. It is climate-relevant as part of the adaptation water management section, although the quote itself is institutional.

policy_statement: Qatar is restoring marine habitats by growing mangrove trees and planting indigenous trees in urban areas to increase carbon sequestration potential.
source_quote: Furthermore, a draft law to regulate groundwater wells drilling has been completed. On biodiversity, Qatar is restoring marine habitats, particularly growing mangrove trees, and planting indigenous trees in urban areas and hence increasing the potential for carbon sequestration.
extraction_rationale: This is a nature-based climate policy using mangroves and indigenous trees, with explicit carbon sequestration benefits.

policy_statement: Qatar has committed to formulating a comprehensive urban development plan and sustainable urbanization and population distribution policy under National Vision 2030.
source_quote: Qatar has committed itself to formulating a comprehensive urban development plan and a sustainable urbanization and population distribution policy. The plan, which comprises detailed strategies and operational aspects, is guided by the National Vision 2030 as a general framework.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning policy with a clear commitment to develop comprehensive urban and population-distribution policy. The climate link is indirect but appears in the adaptation infrastructure section.

policy_statement: Qatar is studying coastal climate impacts, including sea-level rise, flooding, erosion, port operations, structural reliability, and coral bleaching for 2040 and 2100 planning horizons.
source_quote: The results of the impacts of climate change along the Qatari coast for the horizon years 2040 and 2100 is based on the analysis of the future changes of several coastal impact indicators. The adaptation studies focused on identifying the most relevant socio-economic systems, natural ecosystems, and the most pertinent coastal impacts affecting the identified systems. The principal impacts considered to affect the systems above are flooding, erosion, port operations, structural reliability, and coral bleaching.
extraction_rationale: This is an adaptation planning study addressing specific climate hazards. It is more process-oriented than implementation-oriented but qualifies as a concrete risk assessment action.

policy_statement: Qatar has undertaken and planned sustainable infrastructure projects including stadiums, integrated rail, expressways, roads and drainage, sustainable residential complexes, and parking bays.
source_quote: The State of Qatar has undertaken/planned several projects to enhance the overall infrastructure in the country with a strong focus on sustainability. Besides the sustainable stadiums being developed for the FIFA World Cup 2022, several other projects such as the Qatar integrated rail project, expressway program, roads and drainage program, development of sustainable residential complexes (Lusail city, Msheireb downtown), development of parking bays, inter alia hold key to Qatar's plans of sustainable infrastructure development.
extraction_rationale: This is a set of specific infrastructure programs with a stated sustainability focus. The climate mechanism varies by project, so classification is based on the adaptation infrastructure context.

policy_statement: Qatar will use media campaigns and broad engagement initiatives to build climate change awareness in society.
source_quote: Raising awareness is important for the creation of a shared understanding which is required to effectively rally resources and stakeholders for joint problem-solving. Traditional methods such as media campaigns will be used to spark attention and broad engagement initiatives will be applied to anchor the topic of climate change deeper in society.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public awareness intervention for climate change. Its causal climate mechanism is indirect because it relies on behavioral change.

policy_statement: Qatar Foundation is using workplace campaigns such as 'think before you print,' 'save at your desk,' and 'Paperless office' to reduce waste and energy consumption.
source_quote: To target behavioral changes in the community by raising awareness about climate change, institutions like Qatar Foundation, for example, are initiating regular practices that encourage the adoption of more sustainable habits. The Foundation has established campaigns like, the 'think before you print,' 'save at your desk,' and 'Paperless office,' that encourage employees on changing printers' settings to minimize waste and incentivize users to further reduce the energy consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific set of named behavioral campaigns targeting waste and energy reductions.

policy_statement: TARSHEED community awareness activities provide conservation campaigns and school-level training through KAHRAMAA awareness initiatives.
source_quote: The TARSHEED Community awareness activities focuses on various conservation campaigns and basic training at school level, along with the KAHRAMAA awareness park for general public, is aimed to illustrate to the community the importance of sustainable development, and for inception of ideas for younger generation for behavioral changes Other organizations like the Qatar Green Building Council (QGBC) has established a project under the name of 'no paper day' in 2013, that aims to encourage the local community to adopt eco-friendly initiatives geared at reducing waste nationwide and to remind the public that reducing the use of Qatar's resources not only can improve business efficiency, but also help to preserve the environment's long-term health.
extraction_rationale: This is a named conservation awareness and training program. The source sentence is grammatically incomplete in the document but provides a specific intervention.

policy_statement: Qatar Green Building Council's 'no paper day' initiative encourages reduced paper, plastic, and metal consumption nationwide.
source_quote: Other organizations like the Qatar Green Building Council (QGBC) has established a project under the name of 'no paper day' in 2013, that aims to encourage the local community to adopt eco-friendly initiatives geared at reducing waste nationwide and to remind the public that reducing the use of Qatar's resources not only can improve business efficiency, but also help to preserve the environment's long-term health. The initiative is part of QGBC's efforts to help schools, companies, and institutions, find ways to reduce paper, plastic and metal consumption, engage the wider community in environmentally friendly practices, and raise sustainability awareness.
extraction_rationale: This is a named waste-reduction and resource-use awareness initiative with specific target materials.

policy_statement: Qatar has launched a national food security strategy to optimize agricultural land and water resources and protect domestic food needs from shocks.
source_quote: Qatar has launched a robust national food security strategy to optimize the use of the country's agricultural land and water resources and insulate domestic food needs from external shocks. This is increasingly important especially as rising weather-related disasters could disrupt the yields and provision of major crops, impacting Qatar's already challenging agriculture landscape. The strategy focuses on four pillars of enhancing international trade and logistics, increasing domestic selfsufficiency in some niches, building strategic reserves and enhancing domestic markets.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national strategy with four explicit pillars, so it is extracted as a parent policy with sub-policies. It is adaptation-focused because it addresses shocks and weather-related disasters.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Under the food security strategy, Qatar is diversifying trade partners for critical commodities and establishing contingency plans to reduce exposure to trade shocks and disruptions.
source_quote: Under the first pillar of international trade and logistics, Qatar is geographically diversifying trade partners for critical commodities to reduce exposure to external shocks. In addition, Qatar has also proactively put in place contingency plans to limit impacts of trade shocks or other exogenous disruptions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation action under the strategy's first pillar, aimed at reducing food-system vulnerability to external shocks.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Under the food security strategy, Qatar will increase domestic self-sufficiency in vegetables, red meat, and fisheries while reducing groundwater-based fodder production.
source_quote: Qatar has also made huge strides to increase the domestic self-sufficiency of its vegetables, red meat and fisheries production, as well as reducing groundwater-based fodder production. For vegetables production, it has plans to develop its hydroponics greenhouse cluster to reach 70% self-sufficiency on greenhouse vegetables and has launched multiple programs and subsidies towards greenhouse production.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific food-security adaptation action with a quantified 70% self-sufficiency target and a groundwater conservation component.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Qatar has launched programs and subsidies for greenhouse production to support hydroponic greenhouse development and 70% self-sufficiency in greenhouse vegetables.
source_quote: For vegetables production, it has plans to develop its hydroponics greenhouse cluster to reach 70% self-sufficiency on greenhouse vegetables and has launched multiple programs and subsidies towards greenhouse production. Such initiatives will not only ensure that the country is well adapted to potential shocks, but also contribute towards more sustainable agriculture practices including better optimization of agrochemicals usage and water efficiency. This should also help decrease the transportation CO2 footprint of the food offered in the country.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific subsidy/program package with a quantified self-sufficiency target. It is classified as a financial instrument because subsidies are explicitly included.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Under the food security strategy, Qatar plans to establish reserves of perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water, and groundwater to buffer production disruptions.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to put in place adequate reserves, including perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water and groundwater reserves to buffer against potential production disruptions. Lastly, it is also building transparency and efficiency in its domestic market through farmer support programs, food waste programs and food standards governance initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific resilience measure for food and water supply continuity under the strategy.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Under the food security strategy, Qatar is improving domestic market transparency and efficiency through farmer support programs, food waste programs, and food standards governance initiatives.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to put in place adequate reserves, including perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water and groundwater reserves to buffer against potential production disruptions. Lastly, it is also building transparency and efficiency in its domestic market through farmer support programs, food waste programs and food standards governance initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific set of programs and governance initiatives under the food security strategy; it is climate-relevant through adaptation and efficiency of the food system.

policy_statement: Qatar will design a National Measurement, Reporting and Verification system to measure and validate progress toward NDC commitments using verified sector-specific MRV communications.
source_quote: Governed by the MME Climate Change Department, the National Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System will be designed to measure and validate progress towards the commitments made in this NDC, using verified sector specific MRV communications prepared by the national stakeholders. Effective MRV processes are key to guarantee best practice accounting, transparency, precision and comparability on climate change information. The three pillars of Qatar's MRV process are as follows:
extraction_rationale: This is a named climate governance and accountability system followed by three stated pillars, so it is extracted as a parent policy. It directly supports implementation and verification of climate commitments rather than reducing emissions by itself.

parent_statement: National Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System
policy_statement: Under the MRV system, Qatar will derive data for a national GHG inventory and estimate national GHG emissions using direct measurement, calculations, estimates, and IPCC inventory guidelines.
source_quote: Measurement requires the derivation of data for a national GHG inventory and estimation of national GHG emissions through both direct measurement using devices, complemented by calculations and estimates. In order to ensure high quality of the data, all calculations will follow strict guidance using IPCC guidelines for National GHG inventories.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific measurement pillar of the MRV system, with a concrete commitment to national GHG inventory data and IPCC-guided calculations.

parent_statement: National Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System
policy_statement: Under the MRV system, Qatar will compile and submit reports and documentation on measurement results, including methodologies, assumptions, and data.
source_quote: Reporting refers to compilation of required reports, submission to respective stakeholders (i.e. UNFCCC) and preparation of the necessary documentation of measurement results to inform all interested parties. In order to achieve a high level of transparency, the reporting does not only include results but also methodologies, assumptions and data.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific reporting pillar of the MRV system, including concrete reporting outputs and transparency requirements.

parent_statement: National Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System
policy_statement: Under the MRV system, Qatar will use third-party accredited entities to review and validate generated data and reports and incorporate findings into continuous MRV improvement.
source_quote: Verification is essential for a thorough MRV process and incorporates review and validation of the generated data and reports by third party accredited entities to ensure the quality of measurement and reporting. Review will be conducted, and findings will be incorporated into the MRV process to ensure continuous improvement.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific verification pillar of the MRV system with third-party validation and continuous-improvement mechanisms.

policy_statement: Singapore pledged to reduce emissions intensity by 36 percent from 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
source_quote: In 2009, Singapore pledged to reduce emissions by 16 per cent from business-as-usual (BAU) levels by 2020. In 2015, building on our earlier commitment, Singapore pledged to reduce our Emissions Intensity 11  (EI) by 36 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030, and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
section_header: SINGAPORE'S COMMITMENTS TO ADDRESS CLIMATE CHANGE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national emissions-intensity target with a deadline and peaking aim.

policy_statement: Singapore switched power generation from fuel oil to natural gas and prices energy at market cost without subsidy.
source_quote: We made early policy choices that reduced our GHG emissions, for example by switching from fuel oil to natural gas the cleanest form of fossil fuel - for power generation. Today, about 95 per cent of our electricity is generated from natural gas. We also price energy at market cost, without any subsidy, so that households and businesses will use energy judiciously.
section_header: SINGAPORE'S NATIONAL CIRCUMSTANCES AND EARLY ACTIONS
extraction_rationale: This identifies deliberate fuel-switching and energy-pricing policies with stated GHG-reduction and energy-use effects.

policy_statement: NEA and EDB will work with manufacturing industries to achieve energy-efficiency improvement rates comparable to 1 to 2 percent per year and regularly review the Energy Conservation Act.
source_quote: The National Environment Agency (NEA) and Economic Development Board (EDB) will work with the manufacturing sector industries to achieve energy efficiency improvement rates similar to the 1 to 2 per cent per annum being achieved in leading developed countries like Belgium and the Netherlands. Several schemes are already in place to support greater energy efficiency (see next page). The Energy Conservation Act (ECA), which covers energy-intensive industrial firms, will be reviewed regularly so that it remains effective in supporting energy efficiency improvements.
extraction_rationale: This is an agency commitment with a quantified efficiency benchmark and regulatory review.

policy_statement: The Energy Conservation Act requires energy-intensive industrial users to appoint energy managers, report energy and GHG information annually, and submit and review energy-efficiency plans.
source_quote: Energy-intensive users in the industrial sector are required to appoint an energy manager, monitor and report energy use and GHG emissions-related information annually. They also have to submit an energy efficiency improvement plan and review this plan annually.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory requirement for industrial energy and GHG management.

policy_statement: The Singapore Certified Energy Manager training grant covers about 70 percent of energy-management training costs.
source_quote: This is a training and certification programme in energy management. The SCEM training grant covers about 70 per cent of training costs.
extraction_rationale: This is a named capacity-building programme with a quantified grant subsidy.

policy_statement: The Energy Efficiency National Partnership Programme helps companies adopt energy management systems, attend learning events, and receive recognition for energy-management best practices.
source_quote:
This is a voluntary partnership programme for companies that includes:

- Promoting adoption of an energy management system (For example, ISO 50001)
- Organising learning events such as the National Energy Efficiency Conference
- Providing recognition schemes to encourage best practices in energy management
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with listed sub-actions, so it is extracted as a parent policy.

policy_statement: The Energy Efficiency Financing Pilot Programme finances up to 100 percent of upfront capital investment for companies' energy-efficiency projects.
source_quote: Under this programme, companies receive financing for up to 100 per cent of the upfront capital investment of energy efficiency projects. Cost savings are shared between the financier and the company.
extraction_rationale: This is a named financial instrument for energy-efficiency investments.

policy_statement: NEA co-funds up to 50 percent of resource-efficient design workshops for new facilities, capped at $600,000 per project.
source_quote: NEA co-funds up to 50 per cent of the cost of design workshops to integrate energy and resource efficiency in the design of new facilities, capped at $600,000 per project.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified co-funding grant for resource-efficient facility design.

policy_statement: NEA co-funds 50 percent of energy audit costs for existing facilities, capped at $200,000 per project.
source_quote: NEA co-funds 50 per cent of the costs of an energy audit, which assesses energy consumption and helps to develop energy efficiency improvement plans for existing facilities, capped at $200,000 per project.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified grant for energy audits.

policy_statement: EDB and NEA co-fund up to 20 percent of investment costs for energy-efficient equipment or technologies.
source_quote: EDB and NEA co-fund up to 20 per cent of the investment cost of energy efficient equipment or technologies. Besides grants, tax incentive schemes are also available.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified co-funding incentive for energy-efficient equipment or technology.

policy_statement: Singapore provides tax incentives for energy-efficiency investments through ADAS and the Investment Allowance - Energy Efficiency Scheme.
source_quote: The Accelerated Depreciation Allowance Scheme (ADAS) allows the writeoff or depreciation, within one year, of capital expenditure on more energy efficient or energysaving equipment to replace existing ones. The Investment Allowance - Energy Efficiency Scheme (IA) allows an additional 30 per cent investment allowance for energy efficiency investments against taxable income, on top of normal capital allowances.
extraction_rationale: This is a set of named tax incentive schemes for energy-efficiency investments.

policy_statement: EDB and NEA will study policy options to reduce non-CO2 GHG emissions from the semiconductor sub-sector.
source_quote: Although most of Singapore's GHG emissions consist of CO 2 , non-CO 2 GHGs also contribute a small percentage (2.1 per cent in 2012). In Singapore, most of the non-CO 2 GHG emissions are from the semiconductor sub-sector. 18 EDB and NEA will study policy options to support the implementation of appropriate measures and technologies to reduce non-CO 2 GHG emissions from the sub-sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy-development commitment for a named GHG source; it is preliminary because it is a study.

policy_statement: EDB and NEA will study policy options to facilitate industrial switching from fuel oil to cleaner fuels such as natural gas.
source_quote: In the industry sector, fuels such as fuel oil are directly combusted to meet heating needs, for example in boilers. Switching to cleaner fuels such as natural gas can decrease carbon emissions from heating processes by about 25 per cent. EDB and NEA will study further policy options to facilitate this switch.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy-development commitment to reduce industrial emissions through cleaner fuels.

policy_statement: BCA introduced revised Green Mark 2015 criteria to raise building energy performance standards and recognise energy efficiency and renewable energy.
source_quote: To keep pace with technological advancements and raise energy performance standards, BCA introduced the revised Green Mark 2015 criteria. Enhancements include increased recognition for energy efficiency and for adoption of renewable energy.
section_header: A Leading Rating System for the Tropics: Green Mark 2015
extraction_rationale: This is a named building-rating policy revision with concrete energy-performance criteria.

policy_statement: BCA's 3rd Green Building Masterplan will encourage energy-efficient retrofits in tenanted spaces and contribute to making 80 percent of buildings green by 2030.
source_quote: Beyond the existing Green Lease Toolkit 20  and user-centric Green Mark schemes, BCA will step up efforts to encourage the retrofitting of tenanted spaces with energy-efficient fittings, such as light fittings. To enhance current efforts to green existing buildings, BCA and Singapore Green Building Council (SGBC) have collaborated to develop the Zero Capital Partnership 21  scheme, which provides a 'zero capital' solution for building owners to carry out energy efficiency retrofits for buildings. These efforts will contribute to Singapore's aim of making 80 per cent of all buildings green by 2030.
section_header: Building a Greener Tomorrow 3rd Green Building Masterplan
extraction_rationale: This is a named masterplan with specific retrofit actions and a quantified 2030 building target.

policy_statement: The Zero Capital Partnership scheme provides a zero-capital solution for building owners to carry out energy-efficiency retrofits.
source_quote: To enhance current efforts to green existing buildings, BCA and Singapore Green Building Council (SGBC) have collaborated to develop the Zero Capital Partnership 21  scheme, which provides a 'zero capital' solution for building owners to carry out energy efficiency retrofits for buildings. These efforts will contribute to Singapore's aim of making 80 per cent of all buildings green by 2030.
section_header: Building a Greener Tomorrow 3rd Green Building Masterplan
extraction_rationale: This is a named financing-oriented scheme for building retrofits.

policy_statement: IDA implemented data-centre energy-efficiency initiatives including the Green Data Centre Standard, Green Mark for Data Centres, Investment Allowance scheme, and Green Data Centre Programme.
source_quote: Recognising this, IDA has implemented initiatives to encourage energy efficiency in the design, operation, and management of data centres. This includes the Green Data Centre Standard (Singapore Standard 564), the BCAIDA Green Mark for Data Centres, the Investment Allowance scheme for energy efficiency projects and the Green Data Centre Programme (GDCP) that supports high-impact research, development, and demonstration projects on energy efficiency in data centres.
extraction_rationale: This is a package of named standards, certification, incentive, and R&D programmes.

policy_statement: Singapore is conducting Tropical Data Centre trials that could reduce data-centre energy consumption by up to 40 percent.
source_quote: As one of the projects under GDCP, Singapore is conducting trials on the world's first Tropical Data Centre (TDC), which could reduce energy consumption of data centres by up to 40 per cent. The TDC will test the operation of data centres under temperatures of up to 38°C and ambient humidity up to or exceeding 90 per cent.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology trial with quantified potential energy savings.

policy_statement: The BCA SkyLab will serve as a test-bedding, demonstration, and knowledge-sharing facility for energy-efficient building technologies.
source_quote: The BCA SkyLab is part of BCA's plans to accelerate the pace of research, development, and application of innovative energy-efficient building technologies. To be launched in July 2016, it is equipped with state-of-theart features, including a fully-rotatable platform and reconfigurable plug-and-play fittings, for comprehensive tests to be carried out at any orientation to the sun and wind in an urban high-rise setting. The BCA SkyLab will be a key facility for test-bedding, demonstration and knowledge-sharing of green building technologies.
section_header: WORLD'S FIRST HIGH-RISE ROTATABLE LABORATORY FOR THE TROPICS
extraction_rationale: This is a specific test-bed facility for energy-efficient building technologies.

policy_statement: The 2013 Land Transport Master Plan promotes public transport and active mobility through rail, bus, walking, cycling, bicycle-sharing, development-plan requirements, and integrated transport hubs.
source_quote: In the 2013 Land Transport Master Plan, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) of Singapore outlined its objective to make public transport the preferred mode of transportation, and to promote active mobility, such as walking and cycling for shorter commutes and to complement public transport. Selected initiatives in support of this vision include:
extraction_rationale: This is a named transport plan followed by listed sub-actions.

parent_statement: 2013 Land Transport Master Plan
policy_statement: Singapore will double the rail network to 360 km by 2030 and add more than 120 trains to existing lines.
source_quote: An ambitious plan to double the rail network in 15 years. With the opening of Downtown Line 2 in December 2015, Singapore's rail network increased by 10 per cent from 183km in 2014 to some 200km in 2015. This year, the Tuas West Extension for the East-West Line will be completed, adding a further 7.5km. By 2030, the rail network will be 360km, and will be comparable in rail density with developed cities like London, New York and Tokyo. More than 120 trains will also be added to existing train lines, increasing the total fleet size by more than 40 per cent.
extraction_rationale: This is quantified rail infrastructure expansion under the parent transport plan.

parent_statement: 2013 Land Transport Master Plan
policy_statement: The Bus Service Enhancement Programme aims to grow the public bus fleet by 1,000 buses, or about 25 percent, by 2017.
source_quote: The Bus Service Enhancement Programme, launched in 2012, aims to grow the public bus fleet by 1,000 buses or about 25 per cent by 2017 .
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a quantified bus expansion target and deadline.

parent_statement: 2013 Land Transport Master Plan
policy_statement: Singapore will expand sheltered walkways and cycling paths, pilot bicycle-sharing, transform Ang Mo Kio into a model walking and cycling town, and require private developers to consider pedestrians and cyclists.
source_quote: To facilitate walking and cycling, our sheltered walkway network will be quadrupled from the existing 56km to 200km by 2018. Cycling paths will double from 355km in 2015 to more than 700km by 2030. Bicycle-sharing will be piloted in various districts, and Ang Mo Kio will be transformed into a model walking and cycling town. From July 2016, LTA and the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) will require private developers to consider the safety, convenience, and accessibility needs of pedestrians and cyclists in their development plans.
extraction_rationale: This includes quantified active-mobility expansion, a pilot, and a binding development-plan requirement under the parent transport plan.

parent_statement: 2013 Land Transport Master Plan
policy_statement: Singapore will build seven new integrated transport hubs by 2023 and additional hubs in selected development or redevelopment areas.
source_quote: Seven new integrated transport hubs will be built by 2023 to make it convenient for people to access different transport modes and to enjoy shopping and lifestyle services at the same location. Additional integrated transport hubs will be built for selected areas undergoing development or redevelopment.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete transport infrastructure commitment with a quantified target and deadline.

policy_statement: Singapore aims to raise public transport's morning peak mode share from 66 percent in 2015 to 75 percent by 2030 and 85 percent by 2050.
source_quote: These measures collectively aim to increase the use of public transport as a share of overall transport during morning peak hours from 66 per cent in 2015 to 75 per cent by 2030. By 2050, the aim is to further increase this share to 85 per cent.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport mode-share target with deadlines.

policy_statement: By 2030, every HDB town will have a dedicated cycling network.
source_quote: By 2050, the aim is to further increase this share to 85 per cent. By 2030, every HDB town will have a dedicated cycling network.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified active-mobility infrastructure target with a deadline.

policy_statement: Singapore uses COE, ERP, high vehicle taxes, registration fees, and fuel duties to curb vehicle population growth and private transport use.
source_quote: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) systems have been in place for many years to curb the growth of the vehicle population and the use of private transport. This is supplemented by high vehicle taxes, registration fees and fuel duties.
extraction_rationale: This is a set of binding transport pricing and tax instruments; climate relevance is indirect because the stated purpose is demand management.

policy_statement: Phase 2 of the Electric Vehicle Pilot Programme will trial fleet-based EV operations with up to 1,000 EVs and up to 2,000 charging kiosks.
source_quote: Various trials are underway to assess the implementation of electric vehicles (EV) in Singapore. In the first phase, 89 EVs were deployed between 2011 and 2013. In the second phase, the use of EVs will be trialled for fleet-based operations. An EV car-sharing pilot programme for this phase will introduce as many as 1,000 EVs and an island-wide charging infrastructure comprising up to 2,000 charging kiosks to support the eventual proliferation of EVs.
extraction_rationale: This is a named pilot with quantified EV and charging-infrastructure deployment.

policy_statement: IDA and SPRING Singapore announced a $20 million pilot project to develop an integrated delivery system for malls.
source_quote: In 2015, IDA and SPRING Singapore announced a $20 million pilot project to develop an integrated delivery system for malls. If scaled to cover all of Singapore's malls, such consolidation and coordination could reduce the number of trucks on the road by 25 per cent, reduce waiting time for deliveries by 65 per cent, reduce the manpower required for deliveries by 40 per cent, and result in lower carbon emissions from trucks.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded pilot with quantified logistics-efficiency outcomes and stated carbon-emissions benefit.

policy_statement: The Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme gives incentives for low-emission vehicles and registration surcharges for high-emission vehicles based on CO2/km performance.
source_quote: The Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme (CEVS) was introduced in January 2013. The scheme applies to all new cars, taxis and newly-imported used cars that are registered in Singapore. Under the CEVS, these vehicles are divided into categories based on their CO 2 /km performance. Low-emission cars are given incentives, while high-emission cars incur a penalty in the form of a registration surcharge.
section_header: ENCOURAGING THE SHIFT TO MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLES
extraction_rationale: This is a named vehicle emissions pricing instrument tied to CO2/km.

policy_statement: The Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme will be reviewed in 2017.
source_quote: The rebates and surcharges are applied upfront at the point of purchase, to have a more significant impact on consumers' purchase decisions, and encourage them to choose lower-emission car and taxi models. The CEVS will be reviewed in 2017.
section_header: ENCOURAGING THE SHIFT TO MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLES

policy_statement: The Fuel Economy Labeling Scheme provides fuel-performance information to support fuel-efficient vehicle choices.
source_quote: The Fuel Economy Labeling Scheme (FELS) introduced in 2012 complements the CEVS by providing information on the fuel performance of each car model. Together, the CEVS and FELS allow consumers to choose fuel-efficient cars, which in turn leads to savings on fuel cost and lower carbon emissions.
section_header: ENCOURAGING THE SHIFT TO MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLES
extraction_rationale: This is a named consumer information scheme for vehicle fuel efficiency.
